sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents from simple chatbots to autonomous systems capable of multi-step reasoning and tool use. Highlighted how LangGraph enables developers to build reliable agent workflows with state management and human-in-the-loop capabilities.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Co-creator of Django, AI researcher
sources.post_summary: Shared insights on the current state of AI infrastructure, noting that while models are commoditizing, the real moat is in data pipelines, evaluation frameworks, and production deployment tooling. Warned against over-investing in model training vs. robust infrastructure.

sources.author: Kelvin Liew
sources.headline: Head of AI @ Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how Notion is integrating AI agents for document automation and workflow orchestration. Shared metrics showing 40% reduction in manual tasks for power users through agent-driven content generation and database management.

sources.author: Sully Omar
sources.headline: Founder @ Replit
sources.post_summary: Announced new AI-powered infrastructure features in Replit including autonomous code deployment agents and real-time collaboration with AI pair programmers. Emphasized the shift from code completion to full project automation.

sources.author: Sarah Guo
sources.headline: Founder @ Conviction, ex-Greylock
sources.post_summary: Analyzed the AI infrastructure investment landscape, arguing that the next 18 months will see massive spending on evaluation platforms, observability tools, and agent orchestration frameworks rather than new foundation models.

sources.author: Elena Rodriguez
sources.headline: GTM Engineer @ Ramp | Ex-Salesforce
sources.post_summary: Discussed building a GTM engineering function that combines product, marketing, and sales data to create automated outbound sequences. Shared how her team reduced CAC by 23% by implementing intent-based triggers and dynamic content personalization.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations @ Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how his RevOps team built a unified attribution model across paid, content, and outbound channels. Highlighted the importance of aligning sales ops tooling with content strategy to improve pipeline predictability.

sources.author: Priya Patel
sources.headline: Founder @ OutboundOS | GTM Advisor
sources.post_summary: Shared a framework for outbound automation that integrates buying signals with personalized multi-touch sequences. Emphasized that successful outbound isn't about volume but about engineering the right context at each stage of the buyer journey.

sources.author: David Kim
sources.headline: VP Sales Operations @ Rippling
sources.post_summary: Detailed how his team operationalized content strategy by creating modular assets that sales reps can dynamically insert into sequences based on prospect signals. Showed 31% improvement in reply rates from this approach.

sources.author: Alex Finn
sources.headline: Solo Founder @ Finny | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Shared the journey of building and launching Finny, a personal finance tool, entirely solo over 4 months. Highlighted key learnings around validating ideas quickly, handling customer support alone, and the emotional rollercoaster of solo development.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: Founder & Engineer @ Notion Templates Co.
sources.post_summary: Posted about pivoting from marketing to full-time indie hacking after teaching herself to code during evenings. Detailed shipping her first paid Notion template product and the unexpected challenges of pricing and marketing as a technical founder.

sources.author: Marcus Lee
sources.headline: Building @ DevFlow | Writing about solo dev life
sources.post_summary: Documented shipping version 2 of his developer productivity tool after 6 weeks of focused building. Broke down the tech decisions, user feedback loop, and how he balanced a full-time job while shipping consistently in public.

sources.author: Elena Voss
sources.headline: Ex-Lawyer turned Software Engineer | Now @ Early-stage startup
sources.post_summary: Shared her transition story from practicing law to becoming a software engineer through self-study and bootcamps. Focused on the mindset shifts, imposter syndrome battles, and first product she contributed to as a junior dev.

sources.author: Jamal Wright
sources.headline: Founder of Taskly | Shipping in public
sources.post_summary: Posted weekly updates on building Taskly, a minimalist task app for freelancers. Covered user acquisition experiments, feature prioritization decisions, and the realities of balancing product development with customer interviews.
